en.name: ChefCount
en.short_description: Track what is in your kitchen and see which recipes you can cook now
en.subtitle: Kitchen stock and recipes
en.promotional_text: Add what you have, and the recipe list reorders to put what you can actually cook tonight at the top. Works offline, no account.
en.description:
ChefCount keeps a list of what is actually in your kitchen and shows you which of its recipes you can cook with it.

YOUR KITCHEN
Add ingredients from a searchable list of 35 staples, or type in a name of your own. Each item carries a quantity, a unit and an optional use-by date that is pre-filled with a typical shelf life for that ingredient. The Kitchen tab groups everything into seven categories, badges each item as expired, due today or with the days remaining, and gathers anything due within three days under a Use soon banner.

RECIPES
Twelve recipes are built into the app. Each one is ranked by how much of it you already hold, so the list reorders itself as your kitchen changes. A recipe card shows how many of its ingredients you have and names the ones you are missing. Open it for the numbered method, servings, calories and the prep and cook times. You can filter the list by breakfast, lunch, dinner or snack.

FRIDGE PHOTO
You can attach one photo of your fridge as a visual reminder. It is written to your device and nothing reads it. ChefCount has no image recognition and does not analyse the picture, detect ingredients from it, or send it anywhere.

WHAT TO EXPECT
ChefCount works entirely offline and needs no account or sign-in. Your inventory is saved on the device and is still there when you come back. The recipes and the staple ingredient list are built into the app, so it does not download new ones. There are no ads and nothing to buy. The interface is in English.

review_information.notes:
No account, no sign-in, and no network connection is needed. All four tabs (Scan, Recipes, Kitchen, Profile) work offline from first launch.

Please note before testing the Scan tab: the "Camera" and "Gallery" buttons do not open the camera or the photo library, and the app requests no camera or photos permission — it has no camera or image-picker dependency at all. Tapping either button runs a 1.2-second animation and then returns four to eight ingredients chosen deterministically from a bundled list of 15. No photo is taken, read, uploaded or analysed. It is a bundled demonstration of the recipe features, not image recognition, and it behaves identically in the simulator and on a device.

Everything downstream of that is real, local logic: Recipes ranks 12 bundled recipes by how much of the current ingredient list each one uses, opens to full steps and timings, Kitchen keeps an editable inventory with expiry days (you can add items by hand there without scanning), and Profile totals the same data.

The grocery and kitchen-tool prices are affiliate links that open a retailer page in the external browser. Nothing else in the app fetches anything; all of its content is compiled in.
